title: Design the system first, the pages second
excerpt: Most identity projects fail quietly, a year later, when the tenth person has to make the hundredth thing. How I plan for that person.
content:
Most identity projects fail quietly, a year after launch, when the tenth person has to make the hundredth thing and the guidelines have no answer. The logo was never the problem. The system was.

Start with the awkward formats

I begin with the pieces nobody puts in a case study: the invoice, the delivery label, the job advert, the slide with too much text. If the idea survives those, the hero image will take care of itself.

  • One typeface that does the work of three
  • A grid that still holds when the text doubles
  • Colour rules short enough to remember

Hand over less

A forty-page guideline is a sign that the system is too complicated. The ones that get used fit on a poster by the printer. I aim for six rules and a folder of real examples.
